patient.chief_complaint: Sudden severe headache while defecating, brought by EMS - patient was found confused by neighbor
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Parker is a 52-year-old man brought by EMS after being found confused by a neighbor approximately 1 hour after being heard calling for help. The neighbor reported hearing a loud thud and found the patient on the bathroom floor. He regained full orientation en route and on arrival. He reports that he was straining during a bowel movement when he developed an instantaneous extremely severe headache. The patient took 1 mg clonazepam (double dose) at home for anxiety before calling his neighbor, which may be contributing to mild somnolence. He vomited twice before EMS arrival. He currently has persistent severe headache, photophobia, and neck stiffness. His blood pressure on scene was reportedly 220/130 mmHg per EMS. He denies any prior similar headaches. He has been inconsistently compliant with his antihypertensive. His alcohol use is notable (2-3 drinks daily). The diagnostic challenge includes: 1) the double-dose clonazepam confounding mental status, 2) severe hypertension making hypertensive emergency a consideration, 3) the patient was found down - trauma must be considered.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 14 (E4V4M6 - mild slowing possibly due to clonazepam); mildly somnolent
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 4mm; EOM intact; no ptosis; no papilledema; pupils reactive
neurological_exam.additional: Definite nuchal rigidity; Kernig positive; Brudzinski positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 3 (somnolence, meningism); note clonazepam may artificially lower GCS

findings.location: Basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures
findings.description: Moderate-to-severe hyperdense blood in basal cisterns
Blood in third and fourth ventricles
No traumatic injury; soft tissue swelling right parieto-occipital - fell during SAH

additional_observations: Fall may be secondary to SAH (loss of consciousness at SAH onset)
Trauma vs SAH - CT supports SAH as primary event
ct.impression: Severe subarachnoid hemorrhage (Fisher grade 4) with intraventricular extension and moderate communicating hydrocephalus. The patient likely fell secondary to the SAH rather than the fall causing the hemorrhage. No skull fracture. CTA required urgently. Consider EVD for hydrocephalus.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 18.4 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 178 mg/dL (H), ALT 62 U/L (H), AST 74 U/L (H), GGT 148 U/L (H), INR 1.4  (H), PTT 38 seconds (H), Troponin I 0.52 ng/mL (H), BNP 428 pg/mL (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 38 cmH2O. WBC: N/A (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 348 mg/dL (very elevated). Glucose: 82 mg/dL (serum 178, ratio 0.46) (ratio 0.46). Xanthochromia: Present. Alcohol: CSF not tested for alcohol but serum ethanol 0.08 mg/dL (legal limit).

ecg.interpretation: High arrhythmia risk. Avoid all QT-prolonging drugs including certain antiemetics and antipsychotics.

findings.finding: Large irregular multilobulated aneurysm 9.2 x 7.8 mm with wide neck 4.8 mm

output.impression: Large AComA aneurysm (9.2 mm) with wide neck and complex morphology. Large aneurysm with Hunt-Hess 3/Fisher 4 SAH. Conventional DSA for treatment planning. Wide neck may require adjunctive coiling devices (balloon remodeling, stent-assisted) or surgical clipping.
recommended_actions: Neurovascular team review for treatment strategy

output.wall_motion: Severe apical akinesis, basal hyperkinesis - severe Takotsubo
output.impression: Severe neurogenic Takotsubo cardiomyopathy EF 28%. Cardiogenic shock risk. Dobutamine support may be needed. Limits vasopressor and triple-H options severely.

output.proposed: Patient requesting clonazepam for anxiety in ICU
warnings: Clonazepam and other benzodiazepines should be minimized in neurocritical care - may mask neurological deterioration
If needed, use short-acting agents with careful monitoring
Patient already took double dose (1 mg) - causing somnolence contributing to exam difficulty
alternatives: Propofol or dexmedetomidine for ICU sedation if needed

output.proposed: Fresh frozen plasma 4 units IV for INR 1.4 pre-procedure
warnings: INR 1.4 mild coagulopathy from alcohol liver disease
FFP correction to INR <1.5 reasonable before endovascular procedure
Vitamin K 10 mg IV can also be given for more durable correction
alternatives: 4-factor PCC (Kcentra) for faster INR correction if urgent surgery needed

output.impression: Day 2 TCD no significant vasospasm yet. Peak vasospasm risk days 4-14. Continue daily monitoring.
recommended_actions: Hemodynamic stability essential given low EF

findings.description: Persistent moderate hydrocephalus after EVD placement

output.impression: No perfusion compromise currently. Hydrocephalus present. EVD is actively draining. No DCI at this time.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Severe aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from AComA aneurysm with hydrocephalus and neurogenic cardiomyopathy (Hunt-Hess 3, Fisher 4)

differential.key_features: SAH pattern on CT not parenchymal; aneurysm identified on CTA
No skull fracture; mechanism (SAH -> fall) more consistent than fall -> SAH; thunderclap during Valsalva is classic SAH
Blood alcohol 0.08 (moderate); CT and CSF confirm SAH as primary event

optimal_actions.action: CT head - confirm severe Fisher 4 SAH with hydrocephalus
Interpret labs - note INR 1.4, troponin 0.52, alcohol markers
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Coagulopathy from alcohol, severe neurogenic cardiac injury, elevated liver enzymes

optimal_actions.action: Analyze ECG - QTc 518 ms critically prolonged
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Critical QTc 518 ms, deep T-wave inversions - high arrhythmia risk, avoid QT drugs
Large AComA aneurysm 9.2 mm, wide neck
Severe Takotsubo EF 28% - critically limits treatment options
FFP for INR 1.4 correction before endovascular procedure

critical_actions: Recognize SAH as primary event, not trauma - crucial distinction
Recognize confounders: clonazepam, alcohol, hypertension masking true neurological status
Avoid QT-prolonging drugs given QTc 518 ms
Cardiology consult for severe Takotsubo EF 28%
contraindicated_actions: Do not assume altered mental status is purely from clonazepam/alcohol without full SAH workup
Do not dismiss as traumatic SAH without considering SAH as primary event
Do not give QT-prolonging antiemetics with QTc 518 ms
Do not use triple-H aggressively given EF 28% Takotsubo
key_reasoning_points: Multiple diagnostic confounders: clonazepam double-dose, alcohol (0.08), hypertensive emergency, fall - all must be dissected from SAH as primary event
Classic Valsalva/straining trigger for SAH: aneurysm rupture during defecation straining
INR 1.4 from alcohol-related liver disease requires correction before endovascular procedure
Severe Takotsubo (EF 28%) fundamentally changes vasospasm management - triple-H therapy dangerous
Fisher grade 4 SAH with IVH and hydrocephalus: highest risk group; EVD placement is critical

red_herrings.data_point: Found down after fall on bathroom floor + clonazepam overdose
red_herrings.intended_effect: Lead clinician to focus on traumatic brain injury or drug overdose as primary diagnosis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: SAH caused the fall (loss of consciousness at rupture); clonazepam added somnolence but did not cause SAH

red_herrings.intended_effect: Focus on hypertensive emergency or coagulopathy as cause of hemorrhage
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hypertension is a SAH risk factor; INR 1.4 is mild from alcohol liver disease; CTA shows aneurysm as etiology
